ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, $ \angle C=90^\circ$, and $ AD$ bisects $ \angle BAC$. Given $ AB=10$ and $ CD=3$, what is the area of $ \triangle ABD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, draw DE$\perp$AB at point E through point D,\\
since $\angle C=90^\circ$ and AD bisects $\angle$BAC,\\
it follows that $DE=CD=3$,\\
thus, the area of $\triangle ABD$ $=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot DE=\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times 3=\boxed{15}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, with a right-angle mark at point C; AC is vertical and BC is horizontal, therefore AC ⟂ BC. Point D is located on segment BC, and segment AD connects from A to D, located inside the triangle. The problem gives that AD bisects ∠BAC, AB = 10, CD = 3. Reasoning: Because D is on BC, and AC ⟂ BC, CD is perpendicular to AC, so CD is the perpendicular distance from point D to side AC, equal to 3. Also because D is on the angle bisector AD of ∠BAC, the perpendicular distances from a point on an angle bisector to the two sides AB and AC of the angle are equal, so the perpendicular distance from point D to AB is also equal to 3. Taking AB as the base of △ABD, the base length is 10 and the height is 3, so the area is (1/2) × 10 × 3 = 15.
